To take a screen shot and save it as a picture

Click the window you want to capture. Press Alt+Print Screen by holding down the Alt key and then pressing the Print Screen key. The Print Screen key is near the upper-right corner of your keyboard. (Depending on the type of keyboard you have, the exact key names on your keyboard may vary slightly.)

Note

You can take a screen shot of your entire desktop rather than just a single window by pressing the Print Screen key without holding down the Alt key.

Click Start, click Accessories, and then click Paint.

In the Paint window, click Edit, and then click Paste.

When the image appears in the Paint window, click File, and then click Save As.

In the Save As dialog box, in the File name box, type a name for the screen shot, and then click Save.
or install screengrab if you have firefox: https://addons.mozilla.org/addon/screengrab/

Hello and thx! Not at all: my PhD was about formal proofs and distributed algorithms.

A formal proof is the successive application of a set of strictly defined logic rules. It's like building a computer program: more precisely in the logical framework I was working on the theorem you try to prove is a certain type (like integers or string for instance, but much more complicated) and its proof is a program of this type.

My thesis was about trying to prove in a formal setting some properties of distributed algorithms: what you can and cannot do when for instance you don't have unique identifier(ip adresses) for each node in a network or when you can broadcast to all the nodes in your local neighborhood and so on. To do this I used the coq proof assistant, an awesome piece of software.

Salut et bienvenue. How difficult is it to become a PhD in France? I mean all the necessary procedures required. I have a genuine interest since I'm a PhD student in another country.

\m/

Hi! There are a few things that are required:

First you have to pass a masters degree, preferably a research oriented one.

Then you have to find a thesis subject. Its usually proposed by a prof. and you interview for the Phd student position. If you get it or not depends on your knowledge of the subject proposed, your grades during your masters degree and the number of applicant for the job. I was lucky because the Subject I applied for was a direct continuation of what worked on during my master thesis and I already knew the thesis advisor.

Then you got to work your ass off and publish enough journal articles to qualify for a Phd. I think it is usually two or three papers published in good quality journals or conferences. Its the hardest part, that goes without saying.

Finally you get to defend your thesis. That is usually a formality because no serious thesis advisor will let you defend if you're not ready, but it is the most stressful part because your thesis examiners question every detail of your work.

that's it! Good luck to you.

Thanks! So basically more or less the same as everywhere. Although I've heard the defense is different in various countries (it lasts many hours in the UK, but is quite short in Australia).
